state.case_summary:
A man in his 70s presented with a 20-year history of progressive ataxia and an 8-month history of 'spasms' in his throat. His difficulty with gait progressed after cessation of alcohol use. The reported throat spasms did not affect his ability to speak or eat.

Examination revealed:- Hypometric saccades- Truncal and limb ataxia - Decreased vibratory sense with inability to ambulate- Bradykinesia and mild rigidity- Palatal myoclonus at a frequency of 1-2 Hz- Patient was unable to stop myoclonus of the palate with voluntary use of the palatal musculature- No clicking was noted by patient or examiners

- Genetic Testing:  Results of testing for spinocerebellar ataxia types 1, 2, 3, 6, and 12 were normal- Imaging Studies:  Test: MRI brain without contrast  Finding: Severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy  Image Title: Axial T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging of the brain and brainstem  Image Description: Demonstrates significant cerebellar atrophy- Video Documentation:  Title: Spontaneous palatal myoclonus  Description: Shows continuous palatal myoclonus that patient cannot voluntarily suppress
